gap: None of the results ChatGPT got gives today's US prices for the whole Jackery lineup. On jackery.com on 2026-11-15, two models tie for the lowest price per Wh: the Explorer 2000 v2 at $999 for 2,042 Wh and the Explorer 1000 Plus at $619 for 1,264 Wh, both $0.49/Wh. The 2000 v2 costs only $330 more than the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 ($669, 1,024 Wh) and has twice the capacity, but it is on pre-order until Nov 16. Jackery's own 1000 Plus page says its add-on battery pack has been discontinued.
standout_why: I compared against GearBrain (HomePower 1000 Plus v2: $749 MSRP and an August intro price of $619, no testing), Notebookcheck's 1500 Ultra launch ($1,399 MSRP and a January $899 early-bird price), Notebookcheck's 1000 v2 launch ($799 on Amazon, August 2024) and 10adventures (an old Explorer 500 review with no prices). Jackery's lineup page shows only '$X off' badges, not prices. TechRadar was truncated, and ProToolReviews and Yahoo returned 403. None of these pages gives current prices across the lineup, price per Wh, stock status or the discontinued 1000 Plus battery pack. All of their prices are launch or MSRP figures.
decides: For anyone who wants about 1 kWh or more for home backup, the current prices point to the Explorer 2000 v2 ($999, $0.49/Wh rated). Using OutdoorGearLab's measured 1,710 Wh it works out to $0.58/Wh, and it ships Nov 16. The cheaper Explorer 1000 Plus ($619) ties on price per Wh but loses because Jackery says its add-on battery is discontinued and its cells are rated for 4,000 cycles, against 6,000 on the v2 HomePower models. The HomePower 1000 Plus v2 ($669, in stock now) is the pick for someone who needs it today, wants to add batteries later (up to five 2 kWh packs) and wants a 23.8 lb unit. For camping, the Explorer 300D ($209, 5.5 lb) beats the Explorer 300 ($289) on both price and weight.

Explorer 100D price: the lineup page lists it (96 Wh, 158 W, NEW) but the store search returned no product.
Explorer 1000 v2 price on its own: Amazon blocked ASIN B0D7PPJZ5J and the Jackery store search returned no standalone listing.
Per-variant availability for the Explorer 1000 Plus and 2000 v2: Jackery returned HTTP 429 to both storecheck and WebFetch, so their prices are the base prices from the search feed.
Explorer 1000 Plus weight: it wasn't in the store text I could read, and the product page was rate-limited.
Measured usable capacity for the 1000 Plus, HomePower 1000 Plus v2, 1500 v2 and HomePower 2000 Plus v2: GearBrain did no testing, and I didn't find a named-reviewer figure within the call budget.
TechRadar's 1500 Ultra article (content truncated), ProToolReviews and Yahoo (both 403) couldn't be read, so I can't confirm what prices they show.
